content.text: In 1864, Grant coordinated Union offensives against Lee in Virginia while Sherman advanced against Johnston toward Atlanta. Grant’s army fought the Wilderness, Spotsylvania, North Anna, Cold Harbor, and Petersburg, suffering heavy losses but relentlessly pursuing Lee. Sheridan defeated Confederate forces in the Shenandoah Valley, while Farragut captured Mobile Bay. Sherman’s flanking campaign forced Johnston from Dalton to Atlanta; Hood’s aggressive attacks failed, and Atlanta fell in September. Sherman then marched to the sea, capturing Savannah, and advanced through the Carolinas. Thomas crushed Hood at Nashville. In spring 1865, Grant broke Lee’s defenses, forcing the evacuation of Richmond and Petersburg. Lee surrendered to Grant at Appomattox on April 9. Sherman later secured Johnston’s surrender.
